# Python Package Signing (PEP 740) -- Reference
<!-- Generated By: Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.6) -->

## Overview

PEP 740 defines how PyPI receives and distributes digitally signed
attestations for Python packages [72]. Uses Sigstore for identity-based
signing. Replaces the deprecated PGP signatures (disabled May 2023) [71].

## PEP 740 Status

- Type: Standards Track (Packaging) [72]
- Created: January 8, 2024 [72]
- Status: Final [72]

## Three Advantages Over PGP (per Trail of Bits)

1. **Identity-based signing:** Uses OIDC identities, not key pairs. Mitigates
   key loss/compromise -- one of the most common PGP failure cases [73].
2. **Verifiable source link:** Signing with upstream source repository
   identity (e.g., GitHub Actions) creates a strong, verifiable association
   between package and source [73].
3. **Verified on upload:** PyPI only permits attestations with verifiable
   signatures. Historical PGP signatures were mostly unverifiable [73].

## How It Works

- When publishing with Trusted Publishing (GitHub Actions), the official
  PyPI publishing workflow generates attestations by default (v1.11.0+) [71]
- The `pypi-attestations` library generates and converts between Sigstore
  Bundles and PEP 740 Attestation objects [71]
- Distributions with attestations get a `provenance` key in the JSON simple
  API [71]

## Adoption (November 2024 launch)

- ~20,000 packages can attest by default (using Trusted Publishing) [71]
- Of the 360 most-downloaded packages: ~5% (20/360) had attestations at
  launch [74]
- ~Two-thirds of top packages had not been updated since attestation
  enablement [74]
- Trail of Bits built "Are we PEP 740 yet?" tracker:
  https://trailofbits.github.io/are-we-pep740-yet/ [74]

## Critical Gap: No Downstream Verification

PEP 740 defines how PyPI receives and verifies attestations, but there is
**no verification flow for installing clients** like pip and uv [73].

Trail of Bits acknowledged this is not an acceptable end state and was
working on a pip plugin architecture for install-time verification [73].

This means: PyPI verifies attestations at upload time, but `pip install`
does not verify attestations at download time. There is currently no way
for end users to automatically verify package provenance during installation.

## Funding and Contributors

- Design and authoring: Sovereign Tech Agency and Google Open Source
  Security Team [73]
- Implementation funding: Google [73]
- Development: Trail of Bits (William Woodruff, Facundo Tuesca, Alexis

## Integrity API

PyPI provides a new Integrity API for programmatic access to PEP 740
attestation data [71].
